Water intoxication results in hyponatremia, restlessness, 
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and polyuria or oliguria; seizures 
also can result. This condition may occur when water is pro-
vided as a replacement for milk, the formula is excessively di-
luted, or bottled water is used instead of an electrolyte solution 
in the treatment of diarrhea.
Minerals
Calcium
Breast-fed infants retain approximately two thirds of their cal-
cium intake. The recommended adequate intake (AI), the mean 
intake, is based on calcium intakes in healthy breast-fed infants. 
The AI for infants 0 to 6 months of age is 200 mg/day; for in-
fants 6 to 12 months of age the AI is 260 mg/day; formulas are 
enhanced accordingly.
Fluoride
